s1.syndrome_frame: a postmenopausal woman with a long-standing, progressively enlarging breast mass associated with skin ulceration
salient_findings: mass is hard, non-tender, and mobile
skin breakdown with mild exudation and bleeding
key_facts: 56-year-old postmenopausal woman
right breast mass noted for more than 1 year
mass has gradually enlarged
mass is hard in texture
mass is non-tender
mass is mobile
skin ulceration over the mass
mild exudation and bleeding from the ulceration
4.5 × 5.5 cm irregular, poorly defined, hard mass
mass is located at the 1 o’clock position in the right breast
2.5 cm from the nipple
no palpable axillary or supraclavicular lymphadenopathy
left breast is normal
breast ultrasound and MRI classified the lesion as BI-RADS category V
chest CT demonstrated a right breast mass suggestive of malignancy
serum breast tumor markers were within normal limits

per_call: Squamous cell carcinoma of the breast

shortlist.label: Invasive ductal carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: most common type of breast cancer, consistent with long-standing, enlarging mass and skin ulceration

shortlist.label: Inflammatory breast cancer
shortlist.why_kept: skin ulceration and rapid progression are characteristic features

shortlist.label: Paget's disease of the breast
shortlist.why_kept: skin involvement and nipple-areolar complex location are typical features

shortlist.label: Angiosarcoma of the breast
shortlist.why_kept: rare, but skin ulceration and rapid growth are possible features

shortlist.label: Metaplastic carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: can present with skin ulceration and rapid growth, although less common

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with a hard, non-tender, and mobile mass, along with skin ulceration and a BI-RADS category V classification on breast ultrasound and MRI, is most consistent with invasive ductal carcinoma, which is the most common type of breast cancer and can cause skin changes and ulceration as it progresses.

rejected.label: Inflammatory breast cancer
rejected.why: While inflammatory breast cancer can cause skin changes, it typically presents with rapid onset of erythema and edema, which is not described in this case.

rejected.label: Paget's disease of the breast
rejected.why: Paget's disease typically presents with eczematous changes to the nipple-areolar complex, which is not described in this case.

rejected.label: Angiosarcoma of the breast
rejected.why: Angiosarcoma is a rare and aggressive tumor that can cause skin changes, but it is less common than invasive ductal carcinoma and the clinical presentation is not as typical for this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Metaplastic carcinoma
rejected.why: Metaplastic carcinoma is a rare subtype of breast cancer that can have a variable clinical presentation, but the described features are more typical of invasive ductal carcinoma.
